key_insight: Increasing the barrel filling ratio from 43% to 53% made detonation-sprayed Cr3C2–NiCr coatings denser and more wear-resistant, despite a slightly higher friction coefficient.
engineering_relevance: Optimizing spraying fill ratio is a practical process lever for improving protective carbide coatings used in high-wear, severe-service components.
method: Detonation-sprayed Cr3C2–NiCr coatings at 43% and 53% barrel filling ratios under the same spray conditions.
Characterized microstructure and phases using microscopy and XRD to compare porosity, carbide distribution, and carbide transformation.
Evaluated dry sliding tribology with ball-on-disc tests at 10 and 15 N and 5 and 10 cm/s.
evidence_signal: The 53% filling ratio coating showed the lowest reported wear rate, 1.23 × 10^-4 mm3/(m·N), alongside a denser microstructure and improved performance at higher loads.
watch_item: The higher-filling-ratio coating improved wear resistance but also raised friction, so application should balance wear protection against possible increases in sliding resistance and heat generation.
paper_title: Effect of Barrel Filling Ratio on the Microstructure, Phase Composition and Tribological Performance of Detonation-Sprayed Cr3C2–NiCr Coatings
